newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM to sign underwriting deals July 5-7.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM to sign underwriting deals July 5-7.

text.p: Polish copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA is likely to sign an underwriting agreement for its 35 million share foreign tranche offer between July 5 and 7, the company said in its issue prospectus on Wednesday.

It said banks underwriting the issue would buy or find investors for the shares and said their stand-by fee would be 0.5 percent of the value of foreign investor tranche shares at the price for large investors, to be announced July 5.
"The (underwriting) agreement will be a base for GDRs issue according to procedures on international capital markets," KGHM said.
Poland will offer 36 percent of KGHM in a public subscription that begins on June 30.

It offers 55 million KGHM shares, or 27.5 percent of the total equity for public subscription, including a 35 million share foreign tranche that may be increased by another 10 million shares if demand proves strong.
The offer's global coordinators, United Bank of Switzerland, Barclays de Zoete Wedd and brokerage Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy will have an option to buy additional seven million shares.
The foreign tranche would be offered to selected investors, it said. GDRs, which will be issued by August 13, will be listed on the London Stock Exchange.
The book-building in the foreign tranche will take place from June 23 to July 3, it said.
It said the minimum issue price for domestic large investors of 14 million shares would be announced on July 28 and the final price would be announced on July 5.
The initial price range was set between 15 and 23 zlotys and the book-building process in the tranche would take place from June 23 to 26.
The privatisation plan also assumes that, up to 15 percent of KGHM would be set aside for about 50,000 present and former employees, leaving the state treasury with 49 percent.
